description:
## Problem
The gate's measuring path (`run_smoke`: `benchbox run` at SF 1 on DuckDB, then sizing the datagen tree) has never run in CI; the job was always skipped. The baseline was produced by calling generator classes directly, a different counting path, so agreement is unproven for tpcdi, write_primitives, transaction_primitives and vector_search, and it is unknown whether each benchmark's power phase passes on DuckDB at SF 1. The 45-minute job timeout and 1500 s per-benchmark timeout have no measurement or owner approval. generator-volume-changes-pass-pr-ci-unchecked-20261112 requires a mutation probe that fails required CI, a measured runtime cost and owner approval of the required check and budget.

## Change
Run the gate for each of the nine benchmarks through `make heavy-run` and record measured bytes against the baseline, wall time and peak memory. Report each disagreement with both byte counts and its cause; the owner picks which side changes. Then run a mutation probe on a throwaway branch pull request that multiplies one generator's output and confirm `core` fails.

## Decision gates
The owner chose on 2026-11-20 to run the nine SF 1 runs and then one throwaway probe pull request. The `MERGE_GATE_EXEMPTIONS` entry for generator-volume is shown to the owner with the table. The owner approves the measured runtime budget and the check being required before #4322 is armed. A benchmark whose power phase cannot pass on DuckDB at SF 1 is reported to the owner, not dropped from the gate silently. The throwaway probe pull request is closed unmerged.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a nine-row table (benchmark, baseline bytes, measured bytes, drift, seconds, peak GiB) with heavy-run log paths; the probe pull request's failing `core` run URL; the owner's budget approval recorded on this item.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
Accepted by the owner in the choice dialog: the agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
Review threads: the accepted text also said the agent never resolves a thread. Asked afterwards which rule applies, the owner chose: "The morning rule: I may resolve a thread once the bot has reviewed the new head and did not raise the finding again." ('I' is the agent.) So the agent pushes the fix and replies, and resolves a thread only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise that finding again.
